# Bounded minimatch backport with legacy CommonJS calls

This local fork retains upstream `minimatch@10.2.6` and its regular-expression APIs, with the bounded preprocessing fix backported from 11.0.1. Version 11 removed `makeRe`, which existing ESLint consumers still use. The entry adds a callable CommonJS export for older glob/ESLint/ExcelJS dependencies, preserving upstream named/class exports and callable defaults. No matching algorithm is reimplemented. Original package integrity, source and precise changes are recorded in PROVENANCE.json; the upstream licence is retained in LICENSE.

The upstream fix bounds globparts preprocessing amplification: [GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249), [upstream change](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/commit/77a0f5c), [11.0.1 release](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch/releases/tag/v11.0.1). First-phase growth stops at braceExpandMax and quadratic deduplication is skipped above 1,000 patterns. The local fork is not audited as an unchanged registry package: the provenance and security regression explicitly cover the backport. No audit allowlist, severity downgrade or advisory suppression is used. Replace the fork when upstream consumers can migrate together to a compatible patched registry release.

`tests/minimatch-compat.test.ts` covers both export styles, defaults and a bounded child-process amplification regression. Full lint/build and report/export tests exercise the actual consumers. The Docker dependency stage copies vendor sources so the file dependency is available in clean production builds.
